newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin praises Russia-NATO planned accord.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin praises Russia-NATO planned accord.

text.p: The accord Russia and NATO plan to sign on Tuesday protects Russia's national interests and minimises the negative consequences of NATO's expansion, Russian President Boris Yeltsin told Itar-Tass news agency on Monday.

But Yeltsin, who is due to leave for Paris later on Monday to sign the Founding Act between Moscow and the Western defence alliance, also reiterated Moscow's general opposition to NATO's plans to invite new members, Tass said.
Yeltsin said the accord contained binding guarantees that NATO would not post nuclear weapons or build up its forces on the territory of the new members it takes in from the former Soviet bloc.
"We managed to secure in the document an obligation, I stress obligation, that such weapons would not be posted there and there would be no preparations to do so," Tass quoted Yeltsin as saying.
"There is firm understanding that there will be no build-up of the forces of the alliance or any additional permanent stationing of NATO forces near our borders," Yeltsin said.

The agreement addresses some of Russia's concerns over the Western defence alliance's eastward expansion but does not prevent the enlargement which Yeltsin once said could ignite the "flame of war" across Europe.
